mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 2% MoM and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL MoM > 0.5% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 10% MoM and S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% month-over-month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE drops > 0.2% MoM and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of economic expansion, a significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.
